# branch squash --fill supplies an empty draft and the selected commit range.

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2026-11-06T20:00:00Z'

cd repo
git init
git commit --allow-empty -m Initial
gs repo init
git add feature.txt
gs branch create feature -m Feature
gs commit create --allow-empty -m Followup

git config spice.message.fill.command mock-message
env MOCK_MESSAGE_RESPONSE=$WORK/message.txt
env MOCK_MESSAGE_RECORD=$WORK/invocation

git rev-parse main feature
cp stdout $WORK/range.txt
gs branch squash --fill
cmp $WORK/invocation/range $WORK/range.txt
cmp $WORK/invocation/draft $WORK/golden/empty.txt
grep '^branch-squash$' $WORK/invocation/operation
git log -1 --format=%s
stdout '^Generated squash$'

# With no external command, filling uses the branch's commit messages.
git config --unset spice.message.fill.command
gs commit create --allow-empty -m 'Second squash message'
gs branch squash --fill
git log -1 --format=%B
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/builtin.txt

-- repo/feature.txt --
feature
-- message.txt --
Generated squash
-- golden/builtin.txt --
Generated squash

Second squash message

-- golden/empty.txt --
